extracted.intended_audience: clinical researchers, methodologists, and peer reviewers evaluating measurement instruments and interrater agreement in biomedical/health research
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and empirical examples for measuring, interpreting, and validating interrater (and intrarater) agreement and methodological-quality instruments in clinical and biomedical research, including recommended statistics and practical considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: MERSQI and NOS-E as methodological quality appraisal tools
rubrics_metrics.description: The MERSQI and NOS-E are useful, reliable, complementary tools for appraising methodological quality of medical education research. Each instrument contains items concerning sampling, controlling for confounders, and integrity of outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation and use of their scores should focus on item-specific codes rather than overall scores. Normative scores should be used for relative rather than absolute judgments because different research questions require different study designs. (Reported median overall MERSQI = 11.3 of 18; median overall NOS-E = 3.22 of 6 in sampled studies.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) for agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: The intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) is a commonly applied measure of agreement for continuous data and can be validly applied to assess intrarater and interrater reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report ICC with confidence intervals; interpret magnitude (example language in text: 'substantial or better (ICC > 0.60)'). Use ICC for continuous measures or ratings that can be treated as interval-scaled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of kappa statistics for categorical agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Kappa-family statistics (Cohen's kappa, Fleiss kappa, weighted kappa) are widely used to quantify interobserver agreement for binary and categorical variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Cohen's kappa for pairwise dichotomous agreement, weighted kappa for ordinal variables, and multi-rater Fleiss kappa for >2 raters. Consider prevalence-adjusted bias-adjusted kappa (PABAK) where prevalence or bias distort standard kappa. Report 95% CIs and interpret values with conventional descriptors (slight, fair, good, excellent) as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bland-Altman plots and Lin concordance for method comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Bland and Altman demonstrated that using a correlation coefficient is not appropriate for assessing interchangeability of two measurement methods; instead use Bland-Altman plots. The Lin concordance correlation coefficient is another measure of agreement/concordance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing a new technique with an established one, present Bland-Altman plots (mean difference ± limits of agreement) and/or Lin CCC; avoid relying on Pearson/Spearman correlation alone to claim interchangeability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic-test interpretation must include interrater agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: In interpreting diagnostic tests attention is conventionally focused on sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and likelihood ratios. However, if the clinicians who interpret the test cannot agree on its interpretation, the test results will be of little practical use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both test accuracy metrics (sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, LR) and interrater agreement statistics (e.g., kappa) for the test interpretation step; lack of interpreter agreement undermines clinical utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geriatric Care Tool (GCT) chart-review dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Pertinent indicators for a chart abstraction tool (the Geriatric Care Tool) were developed and validated according to five dimensions: access to care, comprehensiveness, continuity of care, patient-centred care and appropriateness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop content by consensus of multidisciplinary experts; test intra- and inter-rater reliability item-by-item and report kappa/agreement for each indicator; be cautious as some domains (eg, appropriateness) may show lower reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thresholds used to define 'good' agreement in chart reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: In one validation 3/4 of 169 items demonstrated good agreement defined as kappa greater than 0.40 and agreement over 70%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider prespecifying acceptable thresholds (example: kappa > 0.40 and percent agreement > 70%) when evaluating items in chart abstraction instruments, and report both statistics because each conveys different information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of rater experience, audio-recording, and training on IRR (DOSS example)
rubrics_metrics.description: DOSS IRR presented only fair agreement (κ = 0.36). IRR was significantly higher within more experienced raters; IRR was higher in VFSS clips with audio-recording compared to without; training in that study did not improve and in fact reduced IRR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing studies of rating instruments, consider stratifying or adjusting for rater experience, include audio/video if it can improve shared information, and empirically test training effects (training does not always increase IRR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument validation requires multiple reliability and validity metrics (examples: APROCENF, SPREE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Validation studies reported internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha), item-item and item-total correlations, intraclass correlation, weighted kappa (inter-rater reliability), exploratory factor analysis (construct validity), and inter/intraobserver agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a battery of psychometric tests: Cronbach's alpha for internal consistency, item-total correlations, factor analysis for construct validity, and appropriate agreement statistics for reliability. Report sample sizes and CIs; discuss applicability in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Spearman rho for between-instrument/scale correlation
rubrics_metrics.description: Between-scale correlation (eg, between MERSQI and NOS-E) was calculated using Spearman rho (reported rho 0.49–0.72).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Spearman rank correlation when scales are ordinal or when assumptions for Pearson are not met; interpret correlations in the context of complementary vs redundant instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame-based continuous counting methods improve inter-rater agreement (VGE bubble counting example)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'frame-based' VGE-counting method offers a continuous scale of measurement and showed better inter-rater agreement than the Eftedal and Brubakk grading, even with relatively inexperienced assessors; it had good intra- and inter-rater reliability and potential for computer automation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider designing scoring systems with continuous scales where appropriate and testing whether they improve agreement and allow automation; validate with ICC, Bland-Altman, and test-retest statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographic/digital methods for measuring viability show high reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: In a skin flap viability comparison, interrater reliability for paper-template weight/area and photographic analysis were ICCs ~0.98–0.995 and correlations >0.90; Bland-Altman plots showed no systematic bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digital/photographic methods can offer excellent interrater reliability and ease of data storage/usage; present ICCs, correlation, and Bland-Altman analyses to document validity and absence of systematic bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smartphone teleradiology performance must be assessed by accuracy and agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: A smartphone client-server teleradiology system was evaluated against workstation reads using sensitivity, specificity, accuracy and interrater agreement (kappa) for detecting hemorrhage, ischemic change, dense vessel sign, and vessel occlusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating novel imaging platforms, report diagnostic accuracy metrics and interrater agreement; note study limitations (retrospective design, small number of readers/studies) and avoid overgeneralization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-rater disagreement can change clinical management (AAST splenic injury grading example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter-rater agreement for AAST splenic injury grade was less than perfect (kappa 0.64 for absolute grade) and disagreements could have changed management decisions (eg, ICU management, length of stay, time to return to activity) in a substantive proportion of cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess not only agreement statistics but also the potential clinical impact of disagreement on guideline-based decisions; quantify how disagreement would alter management to inform need for more objective criteria.
